Description: Flowing multi-point mesh gradient (@paper-design/shaders-react). Color slots: colors[] only — no colorBack. Animated (speed). Viewport-exit and hidden-tab pause are built into the library. GPU cost: unmeasured — measure in pilot, do not guess.
Do: Inject brand tokens into colors[] following refero-craft color.md §8 Gradients; honor prefers-reduced-motion with speed={0} (library does not handle it); for screenshot regression pin speed={0} frame={120} for a deterministic render
Don't: Don't ship the default palette — indigo/violet defaults are exactly anti-ai-slop #1; don't run high-contrast motion behind long-form text without an overlay
Code Bad: <MeshGradient /> // default violet palette + untamed motion behind text = AI slop

Description: Frozen mesh gradient. Color slots: colors[]. Static — a speed prop exists but the shader has no u_time uniform (it ignores time entirely) and every preset ships speed: 0. Output is deterministic without extra work. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Use as the safe default for text-heavy sections and for users with prefers-reduced-motion; brand tokens in colors[]
Don't: Don't raise speed hoping for motion — the shader ignores time (no u_time), so a non-zero speed only burns a RAF loop; if you need motion use MeshGradient instead
Code Bad: <StaticMeshGradient speed={1.2} /> // hidden motion in a component named Static

Description: Static radial gradient with focal-point and grain controls. Color slots: colorBack + colors[]. Static. Good behind hero copy where the eye must land on text. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Place the radial focus behind the visual anchor (headline or product shot); keep colorBack within brand neutrals
Don't: Don't center the focus on empty space — a radial hotspot that lands nowhere reads as a rendering bug
Code Bad: <StaticRadialGradient /> // default palette, focus ignoring layout

Description: Soft gradient with film-grain noise that kills gradient banding on large dark areas. Color slots: colorBack + colors[]. Animated (speed). GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Use over MeshGradient when the design calls for texture or a dark theme where banding shows; pin speed={0} frame={N} in screenshot tests; gate motion behind prefers-reduced-motion
Don't: Don't push grain so strong it reads as compression noise on low-DPI screens
Code Bad: <GrainGradient /> // default colors, grain fighting body text

Description: Organic blobs that merge and split like liquid. Color slots: colorBack + colors[]. Animated (speed). Strong personality — one per page is enough. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Reserve for playful or lab/experimental brand moods; brand tokens in colors[]; deterministic screenshots via speed={0} frame={N}; honor prefers-reduced-motion with speed={0}
Don't: Don't run it behind dense UI or forms — blob edges create unpredictable local contrast; don't stack with another animated shader in the same viewport on mobile
Code Bad: <Metaballs colors={['#7C3AED','#A78BFA']} /> // violet slop palette behind a signup form

Description: Ring of slowly drifting smoke. Color slots: colorBack + colors[]. Animated (speed). Calm ambient motion suited to hero sections. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Keep speed low (≤0.5) so it reads as ambient atmosphere not an effect demo; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; pin frame for screenshot tests
Don't: Don't place saturated smoke behind small text — soft edges quietly destroy WCAG contrast
Code Bad: <SmokeRing speed={2} /> // fast smoke = distracting screensaver

Description: Rotating swirl of stripes toward a center. Color slots: colorBack + colors[]. Animated (speed). High visual pull — the eye follows the rotation. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Use only when the swirl center aligns with the layout's focal point; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; pin frame in screenshot tests
Don't: Don't use behind reading flows — continuous rotation near paragraphs induces motion discomfort
Code Bad: <Swirl /> // default colors, vortex center fighting the headline

Description: Warped flowing color field. Color slots: colors[] only. Animated (speed). Fills the whole canvas — there is no colorBack escape hatch, so every color must be brand-correct. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: All slots from brand tokens (no neutral fallback exists); prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; deterministic screenshots via speed={0} frame={N}
Don't: Don't exceed 3-4 colors — warp blends aggressively and extra colors turn to mud
Code Bad: <Warp colors={['#f00','#0f0','#00f','#ff0','#f0f']} /> // color soup after blending

Description: Two-tone spiral (colorBack + colorFront). Animated (speed). The most attention-grabbing pattern in the set. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Treat as a poster/moment element (404, easter egg, campaign) not a daily-UI background; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}
Don't: Don't put near vestibular-sensitive contexts (checkout, settings, long reading) — rotation + high contrast is the worst combination for motion sickness
Code Bad: <Spiral speed={1.5} /> // spinning behind a payment form

Description: Animated voronoi cells. Color slots: colors[] + colorGap + colorGlow (+stepsPerColor). Animated (speed). Reads as scientific/organic texture. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Use colorGap as the brand line color to make cells feel designed; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; pin frame in screenshot tests
Don't: Don't shrink cells below ~24px behind text — the busy lattice destroys glyph edges
Code Bad: <Voronoi /> // default palette, cells too small behind copy

Description: Classic perlin turbulence, two-tone (colorBack + colorFront). Animated (speed). Neutral texture that carries mood without demanding attention. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Good default texture layer for dark themes; keep front/back within one hue family for calm depth; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}
Don't: Don't pair high-contrast front/back with fast speed — it reads as TV static, not texture
Code Bad: <PerlinNoise colorBack={'#000'} colorFront={'#fff'} speed={1.5} /> // TV static

Description: Banded simplex noise; stepsPerColor posterizes the field into discrete bands. Color slots: colors[]. Animated (speed). GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Use stepsPerColor 2-4 for a printed/riso feel that matches editorial layouts; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; pin frame in screenshot tests
Don't: Don't leave default colors — banded noise makes palette mistakes extra visible since each band is a flat swatch
Code Bad: <SimplexNoise /> // default violet bands = swatch-sized slop

Description: Neural-fiber glow lattice. Color slots: colorBack + colorMid + colorFront. Animated (speed). Signature 'AI product' look — which is exactly the risk. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: If the brand is AI-adjacent, deliberately break the cliché: keep glow in brand accent, not cyan/violet; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}
Don't: Don't combine with dark bg + cyan/violet glow — that exact combination is the most recognizable AI-slop hero of 2024-2026
Code Bad: <NeuroNoise colorFront={'#7C3AED'} /> // the default AI-startup hero everyone has

Description: Ordered-dither retro pixel field, two-tone (colorBack + colorFront). Animated (speed). Strong stylistic commitment — brutalist/terminal moods. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Pair with monospace typography and hard edges so the retro read is intentional; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; pin frame in screenshot tests
Don't: Don't drop into an otherwise soft/rounded design system — one retro layer in a soft UI reads as a rendering artifact
Code Bad: <Dithering /> // dither texture floating in a pastel SaaS layout

Description: Volumetric light shafts from an origin point. Color slots: colorBack + colorBloom + colors[]. Animated (speed). Cinematic — dominates any section it is in. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Anchor the ray origin to a meaningful layout point (logo, product, horizon); prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; pin frame in screenshot tests
Don't: Don't run rays across body text — moving bright shafts behind glyphs is the single worst text-contrast case in this set; never stack with another animated shader on mobile
Code Bad: <GodRays /> // default bloom sweeping across a paragraph

Description: Glowing animated border frame. Color slots: colorBack + colors[]. Animated (speed). A containment effect, not a background — outlines cards, CTAs, video frames. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Use on at most one element per screen (the single highest-impact point per SKILL.md Motion rule); prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}
Don't: Don't apply to multiple cards in a grid — competing pulses read as an error state, not emphasis
Code Bad: <PulsingBorder /> on every card // grid of blinking borders = alarm panel

Description: Static dot lattice. Color slots: colorBack + colorFill + colorStroke. No speed prop at all — inherently static and deterministic. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Safe default for technical/docs surfaces and prefers-reduced-motion users; align grid spacing with the layout's spacing tokens
Don't: Don't use as the only texture on an emotional marketing page — it reads as a blueprint, keep it for engineered moods
Code Bad: <DotGrid colorFill={'#7C3AED'} /> // violet dots for no reason

Description: Dots orbiting on a grid. Color slots: colorBack + colors[] (+stepsPerColor). Animated (speed). Data/technology mood with more life than DotGrid. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Use when the section speaks about systems, data, or activity; prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; pin frame in screenshot tests
Don't: Don't raise orbit speed behind numeric dashboards — moving dots next to digits create false change signals
Code Bad: <DotOrbit speed={1.5} /> // dots racing behind a KPI table

Description: Angled translucent color panels sliding in perspective. Color slots: colorBack + colors[]. Animated. Editorial/deco mood. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Match panel angles to the layout's diagonal flow (SKILL.md Layout: asymmetry/diagonal encouraged); prefers-reduced-motion → speed={0}; pin frame in screenshot tests
Don't: Don't use more than 3-4 panel colors — overlapping translucent panels multiply into unplanned colors
Code Bad: <ColorPanels colors={['#f00','#0f0','#00f','#ff0','#f0f','#0ff']} /> // translucent chaos

Description: CMYK print halftone rosette. Five slots: colorBack + colorC + colorM + colorY + colorK — the only shader with a fixed 5-slot scheme. Static in effect: a speed prop exists but the shader has no u_time uniform, so output never changes over time and every preset ships speed: 0. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Keep the CMYK metaphor honest (print/editorial/zine brands); you may remap C/M/Y/K to brand colors as long as the 4-plate layering stays readable; leave speed at its default 0 — a non-zero value only keeps a RAF loop alive with zero visual change
Don't: Don't place behind small text — rosette interference patterns are the busiest texture in this set; don't set speed hoping for motion (the shader ignores time — verified: u_time absent from halftone-cmyk.ts)
Code Bad: <HalftoneCmyk speed={0.2} /> // burns a RAF loop for a shader that ignores time — and default palette

Description: Static wave line pattern, two-tone (colorBack + colorFront). No speed prop at all — inherently static and deterministic. GPU cost: unmeasured.
Do: Use as quiet sectional texture and as the reduced-motion stand-in for fluid shaders (closest static mood match); keep front/back low-contrast for texture, high-contrast for graphic poster use
Don't: Don't fake motion by re-rendering with changing props on a timer — if the design needs moving waves that is a different (animated) shader choice, make it explicitly
Code Bad: setInterval(()=>setPhase(p=>p+1),50) // hand-rolled animation around a static shader
